subject: Launch week surge: temporary rate-limit uplift & proportionate credit proposal
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@nimbushealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch uplift request + ask about credits

Hannah,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We're greenlighting our pilot expansion and the team expects a concentrated burst of traffic during our open-enrollment launch window (April 2-6). Our infra folks did a quick forecast (attached) — peak qps looks like it could be ~6–8x our current steady state for a ~36 hour period.

We need two things: 1) a short-term rate-limit uplift to avoid throttling during the launch, and 2) some form of cost protection — either a prorated credit for the uplift period or a temporary blended rate while the uplift is active. We're not looking for a long-term commit change; this is purely a transient buffer.

Can you confirm what you can offer there? Also, if there's a straightforward way to automate fallback to our smaller model variant if capacity tightens, that's interesting too.

Cheers,
Samira
VP Product Operations
Nimbus Health

Attachments: nimbus-launch-traffic-forecast.csv (text/csv, 23KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch uplift request + ask about credits

Samira — thanks for the forecast, that helps a lot. We can absolutely support a temporary uplift and a prorated cost protection approach. High level options we typically offer for short windows: 

- Ephemeral uplift (72h max): immediate rate-limit increase routed to a transient burst pool; billed at standard overrun rate but eligible for a prorated credit if usage above projected baseline is limited to the uplift window.
- Blended uplift rate: apply a temporary reduced overrun rate for the uplift window (helps predictable invoicing).
- Escrowed credit: Redwood places a credit on the account equivalent to an agreed percentage of expected uplift costs; we reconcile post-window against actuals.

I can put together a short proposal with numbers based on your CSV and route to finance for sign-off. Do you have a preferred approach? If you want the blended-rate path, we'll need a PO or signed amendment; escrowed credit can be done faster and doesn't require PO.

We can also enable an automatic fallback policy that routes requests to a smaller quantized model if latency targets degrade — I CC'd Jordan for the operational details.

— Hannah
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: +1-415-555-0113

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus uplift — recommended terms

Hannah / Ben — reviewing the forecast. Proposed operational and pricing terms to move fast: 

1) Uplift window: 2027-04-02T00:00:00-07:00 through 2027-04-05T11:59:59-07:00 (approx 84 hours) — customer asked ~36 hours; propose we offer an 84h guardrail to cover pre/post spikes.
2) Rate-limit uplift: temporary 4x concurrency/throughput increase, routed to ephemeral burst pool.
3) Billing: apply a blended uplift rate at 60% of our standard overrun rate for the uplift window OR place an escrow equal to 70% of our estimated uplift charge (from the attached forecast). Escrow route avoids delaying launch for PO sign-off.
4) Reconciliation: post-window we compare actual uplift usage vs baseline; if uplift usage <= forecasted spike +/- 10%, we issue a one-time credit equal to (escrow - actual uplift charge). If usage > forecast by >10%, customer pays the actual uplift delta at standard overrun rate.
5) Fallback: enable model-variant fallback with a 10% latency SLACK threshold; logs stored to the customer folder.

Risks / asks: need legal sign-off on the reconciliation language and finance to approve escrow handling. Recommend offering escrow to Nimbus since they want speed.

Jordan
Solutions Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisional-uplift-term-sheet.pdf (proposal, 8 pages)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch uplift request + ask about credits — proposal attached

Samira — quick update and a proposed path so you can move forward this week. Attached is a one-page amendment with the operational uplift and the escrowed-credit path we discussed. Summary below: 

- Uplift window: Apr 2 00:00 PT — Apr 5 11:59 PT (84h guardrail)
- Provision: temporary concurrency/throughput uplift capped at 4x baseline, routed to burst pool
- Payment path: we will place an escrow equal to 70% of the estimated uplift cost (per your forecast). No PO needed to start; escrow will appear as a credit hold on your account.
- Reconciliation: within 10 business days post-window we'll compare actual uplift usage to forecast. If actual <= forecast +/-10% we refund escrow remainder. If actual > forecast by >10% customer is invoiced for the delta at standard overrun rate.
- Operational safety: automatic fallback to a smaller model variant is configured; logs + token-level cost breakdown will be shared in a Drive folder.

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the escrow route and reply with an approver name for the amendment. If you'd prefer a blended-rate invoice instead (simpler for accounting), say so and we'll convert the attached term-sheet to a one-off blended rate — that option will require a signed amendment but we can fast-track DocuSign.

If you confirm escrow now I can have finance create the credit hold and Jordan will coordinate the fallback/runbook with your SREs.

Thanks — excited for your launch!
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0113
